from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        success_circle = Circle(radius=0.5, color="#00FF00", fill_opacity=0.5)

        p_label = Text("p", font_size=30, color="#00FF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[0]))
        self.place_at_grid(success_circle, 'B2')
        self.place_at_grid(success_text, 'C2')
        self.place_at_grid(failure_circle, 'B5')
        self.place_at_grid(failure_text, 'C5')
        self.play(Create(success_circle), Write(success_text), Create(failure_circle), Write(failure_text))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(GRAY), FadeIn(self.lecture[1]))
        self.place_at_grid(p_label, 'A2')
        self.play(Write(p_label))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GRAY), FadeIn(self.lecture[2]))
        self.place_at_grid(q_label, 'A5')
        self.play(Write(q_label))
        
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Formula: P(X=k) = C(n,k) * p^k * (1-p)^(n-k).",
            "C(n,k) counts ways to arrange successes.",
            "p^k * (1-p)^(n-k) calculates sequence probability.",
            "Example: 2 heads in 3 tosses.",
            "Total probability sums these scenarios."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Binomial Formula Breakdown", lecture_lines)
        
        # C(n,k) is not a standard LaTeX command. Use \binom{n}{k} for combinations.
        formula = MathTex(
            "P(X=k) = ", "\\binom{n}{k}", " \\cdot ", "p^k \\cdot (1-p)^{n-k}"
        ).scale(0.8)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "B2")
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        self.play(formula[1].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#0000FF"))
        self.play(formula[3].animate.set_color("#0000FF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        tree = VGroup(
            Dot(),
            Line(UP+LEFT, DOWN+RIGHT), Line(UP+RIGHT, DOWN+LEFT),
            Text("k=2", font_size=18)
        )
        self.place_in_area(tree, "D2", "E5")
        self.play(Create(tree))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(WHITE), self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"))
        self.play(
            formula.animate.set_color("#FF00FF"),
            run_time=1.5
        )
        self.play(formula.animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.wait(1)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing the Probability Distribution", [
            "Bar charts visualize binomial distributions.",
            "Adjust parameters n and p.",
            "Symmetry increases as n grows."
        ])

        # Binomial distribution utility
        from scipy.stats import binom

        def get_bar_chart(n, p):
            x = np.arange(0, n + 1)
            y = binom.pmf(x, n, p)
            bars = VGroup(*[
                Rectangle(height=y_val * 4, width=0.8 / (n + 1), color=BLUE_B, fill_opacity=0.7)
                for y_val in y
            ])
            bars.arrange(RIGHT, aligned_edge=DOWN, buff=0.1)
            return bars

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE_B))
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 1, 1], y_range=[0, 1, 1], x_length=4, y_length=3).shift(self.grid["C3"])
        self.play(Create(axes))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW_A))
        
        chart1 = get_bar_chart(5, 0.5).move_to(axes.get_center())
        chart2 = get_bar_chart(10, 0.5).move_to(axes.get_center())
        
        self.play(FadeIn(chart1))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(Transform(chart1, chart2))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(GREEN_A))
        chart3 = get_bar_chart(20, 0.5).move_to(axes.get_center())
        self.play(Transform(chart1, chart3))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Real-World Application: Quality Control", [
            "Apply Binomial distribution to quality control.",
            "Calculate k defects in n units.",
            "Example: 1 defect in 50 units."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display a factory belt graphic with 50 items.
        belt = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.15, color=BLUE) for _ in range(10)])

        self.play(Create(belt))
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Overlay the binomial formula specifically for k=1.
        formula = MathTex(r"P(X=1) = \binom{50}{1} (0.02)^1 (0.98)^{49}")
        self.place_at_grid(formula, "D3")
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.lecture[1].set_color(GREEN)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Show a highlighted 'Defect' probability result bar.
        result = MathTex(r"\approx 0.3716")
        self.place_at_grid(result, "E3")
        self.play(FadeIn(result))
        self.lecture[2].set_color(ORANGE)
        self.wait(2)

sections.title: Prerequisite Review: Bernoulli Trials
sections.content: Define a 'Bernoulli Trial' as a single experiment with exactly two outcomes: Success (p) or Failure (1-p). Visualize this as a simple coin flip animation: Head (Success) vs. Tail (Failure).
sections.example: Flipping a fair coin: Head (Success, p=0.5), Tail (Failure, q=0.5).

sections.title: Defining the Binomial Conditions (BINS)
sections.content: Introduce the BINS mnemonic: Binary (two outcomes), Independent (trials don't affect each other), Number (fixed number of trials 'n'), Success (constant probability 'p'). Use a checklist visual to emphasize these constraints.
sections.example: A basketball player shooting 10 free throws; each shot is independent with a fixed 70% success rate.

sections.title: The Binomial Formula Breakdown
sections.content: Explain the formula: P(X=k) = C(n,k) * p^k * (1-p)^(n-k). Break it down visually: C(n,k) represents the number of ways to arrange successes, while p^k * (1-p)^(n-k) represents the probability of a specific sequence.
sections.example: Using the combination tree: Calculating the probability of getting exactly 2 heads in 3 tosses.

sections.title: Visualizing the Probability Distribution
sections.content: Display a dynamic bar chart that changes shape as 'n' and 'p' parameters are adjusted. Show how the distribution shifts and becomes more symmetric as 'n' increases (Central Limit Theorem hint).
sections.example: Animation showing 5, 10, and 20 tosses; watch the 'bell curve' shape emerge for 100 trials.

sections.title: Real-World Application: Quality Control
sections.content: Apply the concept to a factory scenario. Calculate the probability of having 'k' defective devices in a batch to demonstrate how companies use this to maintain quality standards.
sections.example: A robot arm on an assembly line has a 2% defect rate. Calculate the probability of finding exactly 1 defective unit in a batch of 50.
